items.title: New study finds no lab-origin signal for COVID-19 but flags 1977 flu

featured_image.name: Scientists discover key clue in pandemic viruses that reveal if they were made in a lab... including Covid and 'Russian flu'

items.description: A study published last week in the journal Cell offers researchers a new tool for one of the most contentious questions in modern science: how to tell whether a pandemic virus emerged from nature or from a laboratory. The research, led by evolutionary biologist Joel Wertheim at the University of California San Diego School of Medicine, analyzed seven major viral outbreaks from recent decades and found that most pandemic viruses show no signs of being pre-adapted for humans before their outbreaks — with one notable exception.[1][2]

items.title: Nearly 700,000 displaced in Lebanon as Israeli strikes enter second week

featured_image.name: Thousands of people in south Lebanon flee intense Israeli ...

items.description: The death toll from Israeli strikes on Lebanon has reached 486, with 1,313 others injured since fighting erupted on March 2, Lebanon's Ministry of Public Health reported Monday. The escalation, now entering its second week, has displaced more than 667,000 people and drawn sharp international concern as Lebanese President Joseph Aoun called for direct negotiations with Israel to halt the violence.[1][2]

items.title: Ukraine says leaked Russian documents show 1.3M war losses

featured_image.name: Scale of Russian deaths in Ukraine signals trouble for Putin

items.description:
Ukraine's military intelligence has obtained classified Russian documents showing Moscow's own assessment of its battlefield losses at 1.315 million killed and seriously wounded since the full-scale invasion began in February 2022, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced on March 10 following a briefing from intelligence chief Oleh Ivashchenko.[1][2]

"We have reason to believe that these figures are understated," Zelenskyy said in a post on X, adding that the documents also reveal a shifting casualty ratio: 62% of Russian losses are now deaths, with only 38% wounded.[1]

items.title: Trump and Netanyahu split over Iran war goals and timeline

featured_image.name: Benjamin Netanyahu to meet Donald Trump as Iran talks reach ...

items.description:
A widening gap between President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu over the duration and objectives of the war with Iran came into sharp focus on Monday, as the two allies sent starkly different signals about how and when the conflict that began on February 28 should end.

In a phone call with CBS News on Monday, Trump said the war was "very complete, pretty much," and later told reporters the conflict would be "ended soon." But at a separate gathering with Republican lawmakers in Miami, he struck a more ambiguous tone: "We've won in ways, we haven't won enough." Hours later, Netanyahu's office released a statement in which the Israeli prime minister warned that Israel was "not done yet" with its offensive against Iran and vowed to continue strikes.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Volkswagen to cut 50,000 jobs in Germany by 2030 as profit halves

featured_image.name: Volkswagen's sweeping cuts devastate workforce with layoffs ...

items.description:
Volkswagen announced Tuesday that it plans to eliminate around 50,000 jobs in Germany by the end of the decade, a sharp escalation of the automaker's restructuring efforts as annual profits fell to their lowest level since the 2016 diesel emissions scandal.

"In total, around 50,000 jobs are due to be cut by 2030 across the Volkswagen Group in Germany," CEO Oliver Blume wrote in a letter to shareholders included in the company's annual report. The company currently employs about 287,000 people in Germany.[1][2][3]

items.title: Tankers begin running Strait of Hormuz blockade as US backs $20B reinsurance plan

featured_image.name: Only a handful of ships risk Strait of Hormuz transit — who made it through  | News.az

items.description: A handful of oil tankers have begun running the gauntlet through the Strait of Hormuz, breaking an effective blockade that has choked one of the world's most critical energy chokepoints since the U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran began on February 28. The tentative resumption comes as the Trump administration rolls out a $20 billion government-backed reinsurance program and Iran issues new warnings to vessels attempting passage.

items.title: US Navy escorts oil tanker through Strait of Hormuz, Wright says

featured_image.name: US offers navy escort for oil tankers passing through Strait ...

items.description:
Energy Secretary Chris Wright announced on March 10 that the US Navy had successfully escorted an oil tanker through the Strait of Hormuz, marking the first confirmed military-assisted transit since the waterway was effectively shut down by Iran's threats following the start of the US-Israeli war on Iran.[1]

Wright's announcement, posted on social media, offered few details about the operation and did not specify whether a broader escort program was now underway. The move comes after days of promises from President Trump and senior administration officials that the Navy would protect commercial shipping through the strait, which handles roughly 20% of the world's crude oil supply.[2][3][1]
